page: Amazon Web Services m8idn.metal-96xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by x86_64 Intel processors. The platform exposes direct hardware access without hypervisor virtualization overhead, delivering 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs operating at clock speeds up to 3.9 GHz. System memory totals 1536.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per logical thread.

Integrated local storage is a defining feature of the m8idn.metal-96xl profile, featuring 22,800 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage. Network throughput is scaled for high-volume enterprise traffic, featuring a baseline networking capacity of 600 Gbps. The server operates without hardware GPU accelerators.

The combination of vast non-volatile local storage, high-density multithreaded compute, and substantial memory capacity enables strong hardware efficiency for dense enterprise workloads. System resources are consolidated onto a single bare-metal chassis, eliminating virtualization latency and providing predictable I/O throughput across storage and network channels.

Amazon Web Services m8idn.metal-96xl is suited for large relational and non-relational database engines, high-throughput distributed file systems, intensive data warehousing, in-memory caching layers with local persistence, and enterprise batch processing applications requiring fast local scratch disks.
description: Amazon Web Services m8idn.metal-96xl is a bare-metal general-purpose instance featuring 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs on an x86_64 Intel architecture clocked up to 3.9 GHz. It includes 1536.0 GB of system memory, providing a standard 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware configuration bundles 22,800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage directly attached to the host, alongside a network baseline bandwidth of 600 Gbps. Because it operates on bare metal without a virtualization hypervisor, the platform provides unconstrained hardware access and consistent low-latency I/O performance across network and disk subsystems. This configuration is particularly suited for high-density transactional databases, real-time analytics clusters, large-scale distributed file systems, and enterprise data processing applications that require extreme network throughput and substantial high-speed local disk capacity.
